x: Of the younger walkers, Jack Rutland and Reg Elson both gave sound performances. Rutland would have done even better if he had not been in the lead early on, and when experience brings more knowledge of even pace, we may expect an outstanding performance from him.
Harry Thaxter did well to finish 12th—our eighth man! Had either Coleman or Rutland been declared as a "B" team man, we should have taken another set of awards, but we must not be too greedy!

A team, unfortunately far from our strongest, competed in the "Leicester Mercury" 20 Miles Walk. Fred Rickards was 4th 2hr. 53min. 20sec.), Rutland 10th (3hr. 1min. 4sec.), Sutton 13th (3hr. 3min. 10sec.), and Doubleday 42nd.

That incredible old-timer Bert East is still walking better than ever and improving with every race. His latest effort is to beat Rutland, McMullen and Coleman in the Club 10. Bert is the Handicappers Headache, how they must love him!
Team Championship.—3rd Cadogan A.C., 45 points. Readman, 5; Rutland, 10; Oliver, 14; Bentley, 16.

It is interesting to note that Jack Rutland, who finished 4th, was at this stage 12th. At 11 miles, Clayton had increased his lead to 400 yards from Charlie, and McMullen and Pat Sapcote had dropped to 4th, with Wright and Bidgood making up ground.

A team of four supported the South Wales Argus 15½ miles Open promoted by Newport Harriers, and the race provided an opportunity for Messrs. Wright, Rutland and Robbins for a reunion with friends and relatives. There was a good entry with 42 individuals and 4 teams.

Jack Bidgood started going up towards the front quite early with Jack Wakeley and Jack Rutland not too far back. Then there followed all in quick succession the remaining five of the “ A ” Team, Don Heath, Hugh McGreechan, “Sir” Harry Shields, Joe Wilson and Dick Frazer.

Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakeley and Readman, closely followed by Sapcote, Sutton and Robins.
